analysis: Dense causal supervision achieved host validation macro HR@10 of 0.510, improving over the previous 0.390 by 0.120 and the baseline 0.505 by 0.005. Category HR@10: Movies_and_TV 0.515, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.550, Electronics 0.410, CDs_and_Vinyl 0.565. Supervising every valid next-item transition plausibly improved training efficiency over one target per prefix, but this single trial does not establish causality or statistical significance. Electronics remains the weakest category. Reported training allocation was 1,081.4 GPU-seconds; no test results were used.
code_summary: Trains one independent SASRec per category: default 64-dimensional tied item embeddings, length-128 right-aligned histories, two causal attention blocks, one attention head, and dropout 0.5. Preserves prefix endpoint sampling while adding dense next-item targets with 32 uniform negatives per valid position, excluding the user's training items. Uses float32 sampled-softmax cross-entropy, averaged over positions within each user and then across users; checkpointed scoring chunks bound activation memory. Training uses seed 42, AdamW, AMP, gradient clipping, and validation-based early stopping. The generated predictor reconstructs the matching architecture and strictly loads exactly one selected checkpoint per category, without averaging or auxiliary scorers.
